email.body1:
BJ, saw Graylog take two Global InfoSec Awards at RSA 2026 and ship 7.1 with automated investigations.

RSA recognition and a major release usually surface more in-market enterprise accounts in the West than a team can personally reach before the quarter closes. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Graylog off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
BJ, quick follow-up for Graylog.

When awards and a release drive a wave of interest, most enterprise teams can't tell how many of those leads become booked meetings before the trail cools. The gap surfaces late, and recovering a quarter is far harder than getting ahead of it.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your West region needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
BJ, last bit of proof for Graylog.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your region's reply rate likely compares to peer security-software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
BJ, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise coverage without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Post-RSA is busy, and timing matters more than any pitch.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of 3 AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise security motion? I'll tailor it to Graylog either way.
